guide_line: Tell a physical change from a chemical change.
steps: A physical change alters form or state. The substance is still the same.
A chemical change makes a new substance. Look for a new color, a gas, heat, light, or a solid forming.
A physical property can be measured without changing what the substance is. Density and boiling point are physical.
A chemical property describes a reaction, such as burning or rusting.
Intensive properties, such as density, do not depend on how much you have. Extensive properties, such as mass, do.

worked_example.q: Ice melts into water. Physical or chemical change?

similar_problem.q: An iron nail rusts. Physical or chemical change?
similar_problem.hint: Rust is iron oxide, a new substance.

problems.q: Ice melts into water. Physical or chemical change?
problems.why: Melting leaves the substance as water. A change of state is physical.
hints: A change of state is not a new substance.

problems.q: An iron nail rusts. Physical or chemical change?
problems.why: Rust is iron oxide. A new substance formed, so the change is chemical.
hints: Rust is a new substance, not just a new shape.

problems.q: Sugar dissolves in tea. Physical or chemical change?
problems.why: Evaporate the water and the sugar is still sugar. Dissolving is physical.
hints: Dissolving does not make a new substance.

problems.q: Wood burns. Physical or chemical change?
problems.why: Burning makes ash, carbon dioxide, and heat. Those are new substances.
hints: A flame that makes new products is chemical.

problems.q: The boiling point of water is 100 °C. What kind of property is that?
problems.why: Measuring the boiling point leaves the water as water. It is a physical property.
hints: A property you can measure without a new substance is physical.

problems.q: Gasoline is flammable. What kind of property is that?
problems.why: Flammability describes a reaction with oxygen. It is a chemical property.
hints: A reaction description is a chemical property.

problems.q: Copper conducts electricity. What kind of property is that?
problems.why: Conducting electricity does not change copper into a new substance.
hints: No new substance forms, so the property is physical.

problems.q: Baking soda fizzes in vinegar. Physical or chemical change?
problems.why: The bubbles are carbon dioxide, a new substance. The change is chemical.
hints: A new gas means a chemical change.

problems.q: The density of aluminum is 2.70 g/cm³. Intensive or extensive?
problems.why: A bigger piece of aluminum still has the same density. Density is intensive.
hints: Ask whether a bigger sample changes the value. Density does not.

problems.q: The mass of a sample is 25 g. Intensive or extensive?
problems.why: Twice as much sample has twice the mass. Mass is extensive.
hints: Mass changes when the amount changes.

problems.q: Silver tarnishes black. Physical or chemical change?
problems.why: Tarnish is silver sulfide, a new substance. The change is chemical.
hints: A new dark compound is not just a color of the same silver.
